def _latest_closed_run() -> str | None:
    from pathlib import Path
    runs = sorted(p.parent.parent.name for p in Path("runs").glob("*/*/county.json") if (p.parent.parent / "ledger.sqlite").exists())
    return runs[-1] if runs else None


def cmd_audit(args) -> int:
    import json
    import shutil
    import time
    from pathlib import Path

    from . import agent, audit, outputs, policy, tracing
    from .layouts import matrix
    from .ledger import Ledger
    from .model import BudgetExceeded, gateway_spend
    from .render import RenderError
    if args.county != "panola":
        print(f"{args.county}: only the matrix layout (panola) is built so far", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    src = None
    if args.resume:
        resume = _latest_closed_run() if args.resume == "latest" else args.resume
        src = Path("runs") / str(resume) / "ledger.sqlite"
        if not resume or not src.exists():
            print(f"no closed run to resume from ({src})", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
    try:
        sources.fetch(args.county)
    except sources.FetchError as e:
        print(e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    note = tracing.init()
    if note:
        print(note)
    try:
        before = gateway_spend()[0]
    except (KeyError, OSError, ValueError):
        before = None
    t0 = time.time()
    started = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S")
    run_id = time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
    out = Path("runs") / run_id
    out.mkdir(parents=True)
    log = lambda *a: print(*a, flush=True)
    phases, sample, summary, stopped, reader = {}, None, None, None, None
    gw = audit.AuditGateway(budget=args.budget)
    try:
        if src:
            shutil.copy(src, out / "ledger.sqlite")           # the run resumed from is never changed
            led = Ledger(out / "ledger.sqlite")
            src_json = src.parent / args.county / "county.json"
            if src_json.exists():
                old = json.loads(src_json.read_text())
                summary, sample = old.get("summary"), old.get("sample")
            print(f"run {run_id}: auditing {args.county} on the ledger of {src.parent.name} (no new read)")
        else:
            led = Ledger(out / "ledger.sqlite")
            print(f"run {run_id}: reading, closing and auditing {args.county}, run budget ${args.budget:.2f}")
            t1 = time.time()
            s_read = matrix.read_county(args.county, gw, led, run_id=run_id, model="auto", log=log)
            phases["read"] = round(time.time() - t1, 1)
            sample = s_read.get("sample")
            if s_read["stopped"]:
                print(s_read["stopped"], file=sys.stderr)
                return 2
        cols = matrix.precinct_order(led, args.county)
        if not cols:
            print("the ledger has no header block (registered voters row); nothing to place columns by", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        geo = matrix.Geometry(args.county, cols)
        chosen = next((json.loads(e["payload_json"]) for e in reversed(led.events(args.county))
                       if e["kind"] == "choose_reader"), None)
        reader = (chosen or {}).get("reader") or "claude-haiku"
        sample = sample or chosen
        gw.model = reader
        t1 = time.time()
        closed = agent.close_county(args.county, gw, led, geo, run_id=run_id, reader=reader, log=log)
        agent.finalize_open(led, args.county)
        phases["close"] = round(time.time() - t1, 1)
        summary = dict(summary if src and summary else closed)
        cs = led.cells(args.county)
        summary.update(cells_accepted=sum(c["status"] == "accepted" for c in cs),
                       cells_cannot_verify=sum(c["status"] == "cannot_verify" for c in cs),
                       cells_document_inconsistent=sum(c["status"] == "document_inconsistent" for c in cs),
                       cells_open=sum(c["status"] not in ("accepted", "cannot_verify", "document_inconsistent")
                                      for c in cs))
        stopped = closed["stopped"]
        if not stopped:
            outputs.fill_boxes(led, args.county, geo)
            t1 = time.time()
            pol = policy.write_for_run(out)
            rows = sources.read_published(args.county)
            fname = sources.file_url(args.county).rsplit("/", 1)[1]
            raw = sources.file_path(args.county).read_bytes()
            res = audit.audit_county(args.county, led, geo, gw, rows, run_dir=out, log=log, run_id=run_id, file_name=fname)
            phases["audit"] = round(time.time() - t1, 1)
            outputs.make_group_crops(args.county, res, geo)
            outputs.write_county(out, args.county, run_id, led, geo, summary)
            d = outputs.write_findings(out, args.county, run_id, res, policy=pol, raw_file=raw, file_name=fname,
                                       file_urls={"scan": sources.scan_url(args.county), "file": sources.file_url(args.county)},
                                       verdicts=led.verdicts(args.county))
    except BudgetExceeded as e:
        stopped = str(e)
        print(f"stopped: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
    except RenderError as e:
        print(e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    finally:
        tracing.shutdown()
    spend = None
    try:
        after = gateway_spend()[0]
        spend = {"before": before, "after": after, "change": round(after - before, 4)}
    except (KeyError, OSError, ValueError, TypeError):
        pass
    seconds = round(time.time() - t0, 1)
    outputs.write_audit_run(out, run_id, started=started, ended=time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S"), seconds=seconds,
                            command="crossfoot " + " ".join(sys.argv[1:]), county=args.county, gw=gw,
                            reader=reader, sample=sample, resumed_from=(src.parent.name if src else None),
                            phases=phases, spend=spend)
    if stopped:
        print("the run stopped before the audit finished; nothing was written beyond run.json", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    c = d["counts"]
    print(f"reader: {reader}; findings: {c['findings']} in {c['groups']} groups; by kind {c['by_kind']}; by status "
          f"{c['by_status']}; values changed in the corrected file: {c['corrections']}")
    print(f"ledger values corrected by a re-read: {d['audit']['ledger_corrected']}; re-reads: {d['audit']['rereads']}")
    print(f"model calls: {gw.calls} {gw.calls_by_model()}; tokens: {gw.prompt_tokens} in, {gw.completion_tokens} out; "
          f"metered cost (estimate): ${gw.cost:.4f}; seconds: {seconds}")
    if spend:
        print(f"gateway spend: ${spend['before']:.4f} -> ${spend['after']:.4f} (change ${spend['change']:.4f})")
    print(f"written: {out / args.county}/ (findings.json, report.md, changes.diff, corrected/, crops/), {out / 'run.json'}")
    return 0


def cmd_verify_known(args) -> int:
    import json
    from pathlib import Path
    known = Path("tests") / f"known_{args.county}.json"
    runs = sorted(p for p in Path("runs").glob(f"*/{args.county}/findings.json"))
    if not known.exists() or not runs:
        print(f"need {known} and a run with {args.county}/findings.json", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.

Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand_col' (small totals add to the grand total) | 'grand_row' (row totals do)
    page: int
    block_id: str
    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
    printed: int | None = None
    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
    ok: bool = False
    printed_key: tuple | None = None   # the printed total as a value of its own: (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
    note: str = ""                     # what is special about this sum (the registered-voters row sits on one sum only)


def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])


def _printed(totals, direction):
    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}


ONE_SUM = "registered voters: this row has no column sums, so its values sit on one sum only"


def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed, printed_key=None, note="") -> Check:
    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed,
                 printed_key, note)


def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "row", k[2]), ONE_SUM if k[2] == "REGISTERED" else "")
            for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "col", k[2])) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_col')."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_col", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grand_row_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed row totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_row'). The registered-voters
    row is not a term: it is not a count of ballots."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        rows = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "row" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block and
                t["key"] != "REGISTERED"]
        if not rows:
            continue
        terms = [((page, block, "row", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in rows]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_row", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.

    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
    """
    blocks: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
        if c["value"] is not None:
            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])


def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)


def all_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:

"""Row sums, column sums and grid completeness. Pure functions: no I/O, no model.

Inputs are plain dicts as the ledger returns them. A cell needs `page, block_id, row_kind, column, value`
(value None means unread). A printed total is `page, block_id, direction, key, value` with direction
'row' (key = row_kind), 'col' (key = column) or 'grand' (key ignored).
A cell is identified by the tuple (page, block_id, row_kind, column), called a cell key below.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN = "TOTAL"  # a cell in this column is the row's printed total, not a term


@dataclass
class Check:
    kind: str                 # 'row' | 'col' | 'grand_col' (small totals add to the grand total) | 'grand_row' (row totals do)
    page: int
    block_id: str
    key: str                  # row_kind for a row sum, column for a column sum, '' for grand
    terms: list = field(default_factory=list)  # [(cell key, value)]
    printed: int | None = None
    computed: int | None = None  # None when a term is unread
    ok: bool = False
    printed_key: tuple | None = None   # the printed total as a value of its own: (page, block, 'row'|'col'|'grand', key)
    note: str = ""                     # what is special about this sum (the registered-voters row sits on one sum only)


def cell_key(c: dict) -> tuple:
    return (c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"], c["column"])


def _printed(totals, direction):
    return {(t["page"], t["block_id"], t["key"] if direction != "grand" else ""): t["value"]
            for t in totals if t["direction"] == direction}


ONE_SUM = "registered voters: this row has no column sums, so its values sit on one sum only"


def _make(kind, page, block, key, cells, printed, printed_key=None, note="") -> Check:
    terms = [(cell_key(c), c["value"]) for c in cells]
    computed = None if any(v is None for _, v in terms) else sum(v for _, v in terms)
    return Check(kind, page, block, key, terms, printed, computed, computed is not None and computed == printed,
                 printed_key, note)


def row_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, row_kind) that has a printed row total: the row's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "row")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        if c["column"] != ROW_TOTAL_COLUMN:
            groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["row_kind"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("row", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "row", k[2]), ONE_SUM if k[2] == "REGISTERED" else "")
            for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def column_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """One check per (page, block, column) that has a printed column total: the column's cells must add to it."""
    printed = _printed(totals, "col")
    groups: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        groups.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"], c["column"]), []).append(c)
    return [_make("col", *k, g, printed[k], (k[0], k[1], "col", k[2])) for k, g in groups.items() if k in printed]


def grand_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed column totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_col')."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        cols = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "col" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block]
        terms = [((page, block, "col", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in cols]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_col", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grand_row_checks(totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    """The printed row totals of a block must add to its printed grand total (kind 'grand_row'). The registered-voters
    row is not a term: it is not a count of ballots."""
    grand = _printed(totals, "grand")
    out = []
    for (page, block, _), g in grand.items():
        rows = [t for t in totals if t["direction"] == "row" and t["page"] == page and t["block_id"] == block and
                t["key"] != "REGISTERED"]
        if not rows:
            continue
        terms = [((page, block, "row", t["key"]), t["value"]) for t in rows]
        comp = sum(v for _, v in terms)
        out.append(Check("grand_row", page, block, "", terms, g, comp, comp == g, (page, block, "grand", "")))
    return out


def grid_gaps(cells: list[dict]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that are absent or unread where the block's grid says they should be.

    Within a block the grid is every row_kind crossed with every column that appears in it.
    Returns sorted (page, block_id, row_kind, column) tuples.
    """
    blocks: dict = {}
    for c in cells:
        b = blocks.setdefault((c["page"], c["block_id"]), {"rows": set(), "cols": set(), "have": set()})
        b["rows"].add(c["row_kind"]); b["cols"].add(c["column"])
        if c["value"] is not None:
            b["have"].add((c["row_kind"], c["column"]))
    return sorted((p, bid, r, col) for (p, bid), b in blocks.items()
                  for r in b["rows"] for col in b["cols"] if (r, col) not in b["have"])


def locate(rows: list[Check], cols: list[Check]) -> list[tuple]:
    """Cell keys that sit on a failing row sum and on a failing column sum at once."""
    bad_rows = {k for ch in rows if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    bad_cols = {k for ch in cols if not ch.ok for k, _ in ch.terms}
    return sorted(bad_rows & bad_cols)


def all_checks(cells: list[dict], totals: list[dict]) -> list[Check]:
    return row_checks(cells, totals) + column_checks(cells, totals) + grand_checks(totals) + grand_row_checks(totals)

"""T03d: the printed sums decide; the corrected file is checked against every printed sum. No network, no model."""
import json

from crossfoot import audit, outputs
from crossfoot.ledger import Ledger
from tests.test_agent import make_block
from tests.test_audit import HEAD, Geo, Gw, file_text, parse


def sm(name, scan, file):
    return {"name": name, "holds_with_scan": scan, "holds_with_file": file}


POLICY = {"question_id": "q", "answer": "cells", "answered_by": "test", "meaning": "m"}
URLS = {"scan": "https://example.org/scan", "file": "https://example.org/file"}


def rd(value):
    return {"model": "m", "dpi": 400, "value": value, "crop": None, "error": None}


# ---- the status rule -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_two_sums_that_hold_with_the_ledger_and_fail_with_the_file_decide():
    assert audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)])
    assert audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, True), sm("b", True, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", False, True)])


def test_a_third_value_from_the_reread_does_not_unsettle_what_the_sums_settle():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)], rd(11), 1, 0)
    assert st == "settled_against_file" and dis is True


def test_made_up_case_the_reread_returns_the_files_value_while_both_sums_hold_with_the_ledger():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)], rd(0), 1, 0)
    assert st == "settled_against_file" and dis is True


def test_a_reread_that_agrees_does_not_disagree():
    assert audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False)], rd(1), 1, 0)[2] is False
    assert audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False)], None, 1, 0)[2] is False


def test_sums_that_do_not_decide_are_cannot_verify_whatever_the_reread_says():
    for sums in ([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)], [sm("a", True, True)], [sm("a", False, False)], []):
        for r in (None, rd(1), rd(0), rd(7)):
            assert audit.finding_status(sums, r, 1, 0)[0] == "cannot_verify", (sums, r)
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)], rd(7), 1, 0)
    assert dis is True and "either value" in why


def test_document_inconsistent_keeps_its_meaning():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("row", True, False), sm("col", False, True)], rd(1), 1, 0)
    assert st == "document_inconsistent" and "row" in why and "col" in why


# ---- the audit makes no re-read where the sums decide --------------------------------------------------------------

def _small(file_early, row_totals=None):
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", row_totals=row_totals)        # precinct 2: early 20, absentee 4, election day 6, total 30
    rows = [["X", "1", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "15", "2", "10", "3"],
            ["X", "2", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "30", "4", str(file_early), "6"]]
    return led, rows


def test_no_reread_is_made_for_a_value_whose_sums_decide(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(21)
    gw = Gw(led, says=lambda r, c, v: 99)
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), gw, parse(file_text(rows)), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    assert gw.asked == [] and res["audit"]["rereads"] == 0
    f = next(f for f in res["findings"] if f["part"] == "early_voting")
    assert f["status"] == "settled_against_file" and f["reread"] is None and f["reread_disagrees"] is False


def test_a_reread_is_made_where_the_sums_do_not_decide(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(22, row_totals={"EARLY": 31})            # the row sum fails with either value
    gw = Gw(led, says=lambda r, c, v: 99)
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), gw, parse(file_text(rows)), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    assert len(gw.asked) == 1 and res["audit"]["rereads"] == 1
    f = next(f for f in res["findings"] if f["part"] == "early_voting")
    assert f["status"] == "cannot_verify" and f["reread_disagrees"] is True and f["reread"]["value"] == 99


# ---- a corrected row is consistent ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def finding(row, part, new, **kw):
    d = {"id": f"f{row}{part}", "file_row": row, "part": part, "file_value": 0, "scan_value": new,
         "kind": "wrong_number", "status": "settled_against_file"}
    d.update(kw)
    return d


def test_a_row_whose_corrected_votes_do_not_equal_its_parts_is_not_corrected_at_all():
    raw = file_text([["X", "1", "C", "", "", "A", "15", "2", "10", "3"],
                     ["X", "2", "C", "", "", "A", "31", "4", "21", "6"],
                     ["X", "3", "C", "", "", "A", "9", "1", "4", "4"]]).encode()
    fs = [finding(1, "votes", 30),                                  # row 1: votes 30, parts 4 + 21 + 6 = 31
          finding(2, "early_voting", 5), finding(2, "votes", 10)]   # row 2: 1 + 5 + 4 = 10
    ok, could = audit.whole_rows(raw, fs)
    assert [f["file_row"] for f in ok] == [2, 2]
    assert len(could) == 1 and could[0]["file_row"] == 1 and could[0]["findings"] == ["f1votes"]
    assert "30" in could[0]["reason"] and "31" in could[0]["reason"]
    new, diff, applied = audit.apply_corrections(raw, ok)
    assert new.decode().splitlines()[2] == "X,2,C,,,A,31,4,21,6"
    assert new.decode().splitlines()[3] == "X,3,C,,,A,10,1,5,4"


def test_write_findings_lists_the_rows_it_could_not_correct_and_marks_the_findings(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(21)
    rows[1][6] = "31"                                              # votes 31 = 4 + 21 + 6; the scan says 30 = 4 + 20 + 6
    raw = file_text(rows).encode()
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), Gw(led), parse(raw.decode()), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    d = outputs.write_findings(tmp_path, "x", "r", res, policy=POLICY, raw_file=raw, file_name="f.csv",
                               file_urls=URLS)
    assert d["counts"]["corrections"] == 2 and not d["could_not_correct"]
    # the same, but only the part is settled: votes left alone makes the row inconsistent, so nothing is changed
    raw2 = file_text(rows).encode()
    fs = [f for f in res["findings"] if f["part"] == "early_voting"]
    ok, could = audit.whole_rows(raw2, [dict(f, file_row=f["file_row"]) for f in fs])
    assert ok == [] and len(could) == 1


# ---- every printed sum, with the published file and with the corrected file ---------------------------------------

def _run(tmp_path, led, rows, n=0):
    raw = file_text(rows).encode()
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), Gw(led), parse(raw.decode()), run_dir=tmp_path / str(n), make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    return outputs.write_findings(tmp_path / str(n), "x", "r", res, policy=POLICY, raw_file=raw, file_name="f.csv",
                                  file_urls=URLS), tmp_path / str(n)


def test_sums_check_counts_every_printed_sum_with_each_file(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(21)
    rows[1][6] = "31"                                               # file votes 31 = its parts; the scan has 30 and 20
    d, out = _run(tmp_path, led, rows)
    sc = d["sums_check"]
    assert sc["in_all"] == 7 and sc["holding_with_published"] < sc["holding_with_corrected"] == 7
    assert sc["still_failing"] == []
    assert "7 printed sums" in (out / "x" / "report.md").read_text()


def test_sums_check_lists_what_still_fails_with_its_reason(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(22, row_totals={"EARLY": 31})
    d, out = _run(tmp_path, led, rows)
    sc = d["sums_check"]
    assert sc["holding_with_corrected"] < sc["in_all"]
    assert sc["still_failing"] and all(s["reasons"] for s in sc["still_failing"])
    assert any("could not be verified" in r for s in sc["still_failing"] for r in s["reasons"])
    assert "could not be verified" in (out / "x" / "report.md").read_text()


def test_a_missing_row_is_the_reason_for_a_sum_that_still_fails(tmp_path):
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", row_totals={"EARLY": 31})           # fails with the ledger's own cells
    rows = [["X", "1", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "15", "2", "10", "3"]]    # precinct 2 is not in the file
    d, _ = _run(tmp_path, led, rows)
    reasons = [r for s in d["sums_check"]["still_failing"] for r in s["reasons"]]
    assert any("missing from the file" in r for r in reasons)


# ---- the same ledger twice ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def test_two_audits_of_the_same_ledger_write_the_same_findings(tmp_path):
    outs = []
    for n in range(2):
        led, rows = _small(22, row_totals={"EARLY": 31})
        d, out = _run(tmp_path, led, rows, n)
        d["run_id"] = "r"
        outs.append(((out / "x" / "findings.json").read_text(), (out / "x" / "report.md").read_text(),
                     (out / "x" / "corrected" / "f.csv").read_bytes()))
    assert outs[0] == outs[1]
    json.loads(outs[0][0])


def test_a_wrong_precinct_group_says_what_a_person_would_do():
    big = [audit.Row(audit.Block("b", 1, "C", "A", cols=["1", "2", "3"]), p, dict(zip(audit.PARTS, f)), 0, {},
                     dict(zip(audit.PARTS, s))) for p, f, s in
           (("1", (320, 14, 168, 138), (181, 5, 102, 74)), ("2", (181, 5, 102, 74), (311, 3, 195, 113)),
            ("3", (311, 3, 195, 113), (320, 14, 168, 138)))]
    for r in big:
        r.block = big[0].block
    slots = audit.classify(big)
    s = audit.what_to_do(slots[0].group, slots)
    assert "3 rows" in s and "precinct" in s and s.count(".") <= 2

    assert audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)])
    assert audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", True, True), sm("b", True, False)])
    assert not audit.sums_decide([sm("a", False, True)])


def test_a_third_value_from_the_reread_does_not_unsettle_what_the_sums_settle():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)], rd(11), 1, 0)
    assert st == "settled_against_file" and dis is True


def test_made_up_case_the_reread_returns_the_files_value_while_both_sums_hold_with_the_ledger():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", True, False)], rd(0), 1, 0)
    assert st == "settled_against_file" and dis is True


def test_a_reread_that_agrees_does_not_disagree():
    assert audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False)], rd(1), 1, 0)[2] is False
    assert audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False)], None, 1, 0)[2] is False


def test_sums_that_do_not_decide_are_cannot_verify_whatever_the_reread_says():
    for sums in ([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)], [sm("a", True, True)], [sm("a", False, False)], []):
        for r in (None, rd(1), rd(0), rd(7)):
            assert audit.finding_status(sums, r, 1, 0)[0] == "cannot_verify", (sums, r)
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("a", True, False), sm("b", False, False)], rd(7), 1, 0)
    assert dis is True and "either value" in why


def test_document_inconsistent_keeps_its_meaning():
    st, why, dis = audit.finding_status([sm("row", True, False), sm("col", False, True)], rd(1), 1, 0)
    assert st == "document_inconsistent" and "row" in why and "col" in why


# ---- the audit makes no re-read where the sums decide --------------------------------------------------------------

def _small(file_early, row_totals=None):
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", row_totals=row_totals)        # precinct 2: early 20, absentee 4, election day 6, total 30
    rows = [["X", "1", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "15", "2", "10", "3"],
            ["X", "2", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "30", "4", str(file_early), "6"]]
    return led, rows


def test_no_reread_is_made_for_a_value_whose_sums_decide(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(21)
    gw = Gw(led, says=lambda r, c, v: 99)
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), gw, parse(file_text(rows)), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    assert gw.asked == [] and res["audit"]["rereads"] == 0
    f = next(f for f in res["findings"] if f["part"] == "early_voting")
    assert f["status"] == "settled_against_file" and f["reread"] is None and f["reread_disagrees"] is False


def test_a_reread_is_made_where_the_sums_do_not_decide(tmp_path):
    led, rows = _small(22, row_totals={"EARLY": 31})            # the row sum fails with either value
    gw = Gw(led, says=lambda r, c, v: 99)
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), gw, parse(file_text(rows)), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)
    assert len(gw.asked) == 1 and res["audit"]["rereads"] == 1
    f = next(f for f in res["findings"] if f["part"] == "early_voting")
    assert f["status"] == "cannot_verify" and f["reread_disagrees"] is True and f["reread"]["value"] == 99


# ---- a corrected row is consistent ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

def finding(row, part, new, **kw):
    d = {"id": f"f{row}{part}", "file_row": row, "part": part, "file_value": 0, "scan_value": new,
         "kind": "wrong_number", "status": "settled_against_file"}
    d.update(kw)
    return d


def test_a_row_whose_corrected_votes_do_not_equal_its_parts_is_not_corrected_at_all():
    raw = file_text([["X", "1", "C", "", "", "A", "15", "2", "10", "3"],
                     ["X", "2", "C", "", "", "A", "31", "4", "21", "6"],
                     ["X", "3", "C", "", "", "A", "9", "1", "4", "4"]]).encode()
    fs = [finding(1, "votes", 30),                                  # row 1: votes 30, parts 4 + 21 + 6 = 31
          finding(2, "early_voting", 5), finding(2, "votes", 10)]   # row 2: 1 + 5 + 4 = 10
    ok, could = audit.whole_rows(raw, fs)
    assert [f["file_row"] for f in ok] == [2, 2]
    assert len(could) == 1 and could[0]["file_row"] == 1 and could[0]["findings"] == ["f1votes"]
    assert "30" in could[0]["reason"] and "31" in could[0]["reason"]
    new, diff, applied = audit.apply_corrections(raw, ok)
    assert new.decode().splitlines()[2] == "X,2,C,,,A,31,4,21,6"
    assert new.decode().splitlines()[3] == "X,3,C,,,A,10,1,5,4"

    raw = file_text(rows).encode()
    res = audit.audit_county("x", led, Geo(), Gw(led), parse(raw.decode()), run_dir=tmp_path, make_crops=False,
                             log=lambda *a: None)

    # the same, but only the part is settled: votes left alone makes the row inconsistent, so nothing is changed

def _run(tmp_path, led, rows, n=0):
    raw = file_text(rows).encode()

                             log=lambda *a: None)

                                  file_urls=URLS), tmp_path / str(n)

    assert any("could not be verified" in r for s in sc["still_failing"] for r in s["reasons"])
    assert "could not be verified" in (out / "x" / "report.md").read_text()


def test_a_missing_row_is_the_reason_for_a_sum_that_still_fails(tmp_path):
    led = Ledger()
    make_block(led, 1, "p1-b1", row_totals={"EARLY": 31})           # fails with the ledger's own cells
    rows = [["X", "1", "C", "", "", "cand p1-b1", "15", "2", "10", "3"]]    # precinct 2 is not in the file
    d, _ = _run(tmp_path, led, rows)

        d, out = _run(tmp_path, led, rows, n)
        d["run_id"] = "r"

                     (out / "x" / "corrected" / "f.csv").read_bytes()))

    json.loads(outs[0][0])

    big = [audit.Row(audit.Block("b", 1, "C", "A", cols=["1", "2", "3"]), p, dict(zip(audit.PARTS, f)), 0, {},
